CHAPTER X

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 58 (1) The Regent conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of Protection of Women and Children.

2. The guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be conducted in the form of: a. training for government officials and law enforcement officers on prevention and handling of violence;
b. training for religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against Women and Children;
c. training for health workers who provide health services to Women and Children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units, and general hospitals;
d. training for social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect Women and Children victims of violence; and f. improvement of professionalism of officers, managers of violence case data against Women and Children at community health centers, integrated service units and hospitals.
3. The Regent in conducting guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) may delegate to the Head of Agency.

Article 59 (1) The Head of DPPPA is obliged to submit a report on the implementation of the Women and Children protection program to the Regent.

2. The report as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted periodically 1 (one) time every 3 (three) months.

Article 60 (1) The Regent conducts supervision and evaluation of the implementation of Protection of Women and Children periodically 1 (one) time every 3 (three) months.

2. The results of the evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) constitute evaluation material for the policy of the Women and Children protection program in the Regency.

REGIONAL HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES

MUSI BANYUASIN REGENCY

REGENT OF MUSI BANYUASIN

DECIDES:

REGIONAL REGULATION ON THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN'S AND CHILDREN'S RIGHTS. CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Part One

Definition, Understanding and Terminology Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regency is Musi Banyuasin Regency. 2. Regency Government is the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Musi Banyuasin. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency. 5. Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as DPPPA is the Regional Apparatus that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Musi Banyuasin Regency. 6. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of Women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 9. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 10. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has potential and/or special talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields. 11. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights. 12. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency/City that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 14. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. Women victims of violence are Women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Child victims of violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 20. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement statutory regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards. 25. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop properly. 26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28.

Part Five

Repatriation and Social Reintegration Services Article 51 (1) Repatriation of victims of violence is aimed at returning Women and Children victims of violence to their area of origin.

2. Repatriation of Women and Children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.
3. The Regency Government carries out repatriation and social reintegration of Women and Children victims of violence in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

Part Two

Community Article 10 (1) The community is obliged and responsible in implementing the protection of Women and Children including:
a. participation in prevention and providing support for the development of prevention programs for violations of the rights of Women and Children;
b. providing information and/or reporting violations of the rights of Women and Children to the competent authorities; and c. supervising the law enforcement process against cases of violations of the rights of Women and Children.
2. The responsibility of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Paragraph 1

General Article 16 The Regency Government implements the Protection of Women by involving:
a. family;
b. community leaders;
c. religious leaders;
d. community;
e. community organizations in the field of protection of Women.

Paragraph 2 Marriage Article 17 During the marriage bond or after divorce, a Woman has the same rights as the man who is her husband/former husband over all matters relating to the consequences of marriage and/or divorce.

Paragraph 3 Health Article 18 (1) The Regency Government provides adequate health and maternity facilities for pregnant and breastfeeding mothers.

2. Public service providers must provide special facilities for breastfeeding mothers.

Paragraph 4 Employment Article 19 (1) Employers who employ Women must maintain decency, safety and security while in the workplace.

2. Employers must place female workers in places that are safe for Women's reproductive health.
3. Employers must fulfill the rights of female workers to receive wages in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
4. Employers provide special facilities for breastfeeding mothers in their companies.

Article 20 (1) Female workers/laborers who are at most 18 (eighteen) years old are prohibited from being employed between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB.

2. Employers are prohibited from employing pregnant female workers/laborers who according to a doctor's statement are dangerous to the health and safety of their pregnancy or themselves during working hours from 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB.
3. Employers who employ female workers/laborers between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB, must: a. provide nutritious food and drinks; and b. maintain decency and security while in the workplace. (4) Employers must provide shuttle transportation for female workers/laborers who depart and return from work between 23.00 WIB until 05.00 WIB.

Paragraph 5 Education

CHAPTER V

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Part One

Implementation of Protection of Women

Part Two

Community Article 14 (1) Efforts made by the community in order to prevent violations of the rights of Women include:
a. monitoring various conditions occurring in their environment that may cause violations of the rights of Women; b. strengthening the role of community, religious organizations and the family environment; and c. prevention of underage marriage/unregistered marriage. (2) Efforts made in order to prevent violations of the rights of Children include: a. monitoring various conditions occurring in their environment that cause violations of the rights of Children;
b. strengthening the role of community, religious organizations and the family environment; and c. prevention of marriage at the age of Children.

Parents and/or Family

Women are guaranteed the right to obtain education at every level of formal and non-formal education.

2. Community Organizations may carry out empowerment for Women experiencing socio-economic vulnerability as referred to in paragraph (1) in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations. !

MUSI BANYUASIN REGENCY

REGENT OF MUSI BANYUASIN

DECIDES:

REGIONAL REGULATION ON THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN'S AND CHILDREN'S RIGHTS. CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Part One

Definition, Understanding and Terminology Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regency is Musi Banyuasin Regency. 2. Regency Government is the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Musi Banyuasin. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency. 5. Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as DPPPA is the Regional Apparatus that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Musi Banyuasin Regency. 6. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of Women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 9. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 10. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has potential and/or special talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields. 11. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights. 12. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency/City that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 14. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. Women victims of violence are Women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Child victims of violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 20. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement statutory regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards. 25. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop properly. 26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28.

CHAPTER X

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 58 (1) The Regent conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of Protection of Women and Children.

2. The guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be conducted in the form of: a. training for government officials and law enforcement officers on prevention and handling of violence;
b. training for religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against Women and Children;
c. training for health workers who provide health services to Women and Children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units, and general hospitals;
d. training for social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect Women and Children victims of violence; and f. improvement of professionalism of officers, managers of violence case data against Women and Children at community health centers, integrated service units and hospitals.
3. The Regent in conducting guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) may delegate to the Head of Agency.

Article 59 (1) The Head of DPPPA is obliged to submit a report on the implementation of the Women and Children protection program to the Regent.

2. The report as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted periodically 1 (one) time every 3 (three) months.

Article 60 (1) The Regent conducts supervision and evaluation of the implementation of Protection of Women and Children periodically 1 (one) time every 3 (three) months.

2. The results of the evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) constitute evaluation material for the policy of the Women and Children protection program in the Regency.

Part Five

Repatriation and Social Reintegration Services Article 51 (1) Repatriation of victims of violence is aimed at returning Women and Children victims of violence to their area of origin.

2. Repatriation of Women and Children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.
3. The Regency Government carries out repatriation and social reintegration of Women and Children victims of violence in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.
Considering Bearing in Mind

Part Two

Community Article 10 (1) The community is obliged and responsible in implementing the protection of Women and Children including:
a. participation in prevention and providing support for the development of prevention programs for violations of the rights of Women and Children;
b. providing information and/or reporting violations of the rights of Women and Children to the competent authorities; and c. supervising the law enforcement process against cases of violations of the rights of Women and Children.
2. The responsibility of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Part Two

Implementation of Protection of the Rights of Children

CHAPTER V

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Part One

Implementation of Protection of Women

Part Three

Parents and/or Family

CHAPTER VIII

CHILDREN'S PARTICIPATION

Article 55 (1) Every Child has the right to participate in expressing opinions, ideas, and thoughts related to life based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity.

2. Children's participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out through Children's Forums starting from the village level, sub-district within the regency.
3. Children's Forums as referred to in paragraph (2) represent Children, both geographic domicile representation, socio-cultural groups and Children's educational backgrounds.
4. The establishment of Children's Forums as referred to in paragraph (2) is facilitated by the Regency Government.
5. The establishment of Children's Forums as referred to in paragraph (4) is stipulated by Regent Decree.

Article 56 (1) In every formulation of policies related to Children, the Regency Government pays attention to and accommodates Children's Opinions submitted through Children's Forums.

2. The Regency Government includes representatives of Children's Forums in the Regency Development Planning Deliberation.

Paragraph 1

General Article 16 The Regency Government implements the Protection of Women by involving:
a. family;
b. community leaders;
c. religious leaders;
d. community;
e. community organizations in the field of protection of Women.

Paragraph 2 Marriage Article 17 During the marriage bond or after divorce, a Woman has the same rights as the man who is her husband/former husband over all matters relating to the consequences of marriage and/or divorce.

Paragraph 3 Health Article 18 (1) The Regency Government provides adequate health and maternity facilities for pregnant and breastfeeding mothers.

2. Public service providers must provide special facilities for breastfeeding mothers.

Paragraph 4 Employment Article 19 (1) Employers who employ Women must maintain decency, safety and security while in the workplace.

2. Employers must place female workers in places that are safe for Women's reproductive health.
3. Employers must fulfill the rights of female workers to receive wages in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
4. Employers provide special facilities for breastfeeding mothers in their companies.

Article 20 (1) Female workers/laborers who are at most 18 (eighteen) years old are prohibited from being employed between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB.

2. Employers are prohibited from employing pregnant female workers/laborers who according to a doctor's statement are dangerous to the health and safety of their pregnancy or themselves during working hours from 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB.
3. Employers who employ female workers/laborers between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB, must: a. provide nutritious food and drinks; and b. maintain decency and security while in the workplace. (4) Employers must provide shuttle transportation for female workers/laborers who depart and return from work between 23.00 WIB until 05.00 WIB.

Paragraph 5 Education

Part Two

Community Article 14 (1) Efforts made by the community in order to prevent violations of the rights of Women include:
a. monitoring various conditions occurring in their environment that may cause violations of the rights of Women; b. strengthening the role of community, religious organizations and the family environment; and c. prevention of underage marriage/unregistered marriage. (2) Efforts made in order to prevent violations of the rights of Children include: a. monitoring various conditions occurring in their environment that cause violations of the rights of Children;
b. strengthening the role of community, religious organizations and the family environment; and c. prevention of marriage at the age of Children.

Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 9. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 10. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has potential and/or special talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields. 11. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights. 12. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency/City that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 14. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of Women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 9. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 10. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has potential and/or special talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields. 11. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights. 12. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency/City that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 14. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. Women victims of violence are Women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Child victims of violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 20. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement statutory regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards. 25. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop properly. 26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28.

CHAPTER X

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 58 (1) The Regent conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of Protection of Women and Children.

2. The guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be conducted in the form of: a. training for government officials and law enforcement officers on prevention and handling of violence;
b. training for religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against Women and Children;
c. training for health workers who provide health services to Women and Children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units, and general hospitals;
d. training for social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect Women and Children victims of violence; and f. improvement of professionalism of officers, managers of violence case data against Women and Children at community health centers, integrated service units and hospitals.
3. The Regent in conducting guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) may delegate to the Head of Agency.

Article 59 (1) The Head of DPPPA is obliged to submit a report on the implementation of the Women and Children protection program to the Regent.

2. The report as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted periodically 1 (one) time every 3 (three) months.

Article 60 (1) The Regent conducts supervision and evaluation of the implementation of Protection of Women and Children periodically 1 (one) time every 3 (three) months.

2. The results of the evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) constitute evaluation material for the policy of the Women and Children protection program in the Regency.

Repatriation and Social Reintegration Services Article 51 (1) Repatriation of victims of violence is aimed at returning Women and Children victims of violence to their area of origin.

2. Repatriation of Women and Children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.
3. The Regency Government carries out repatriation and social reintegration of Women and Children victims of violence in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

General Article 16 The Regency Government implements the Protection of Women by involving:
a. family;
b. community leaders;
c. religious leaders;

e. community organizations in the field of protection of Women.

Paragraph 2 Marriage Article 17 During the marriage bond or after divorce, a Woman has the same rights as the man who is her husband/former husband over all matters relating to the consequences of marriage and/or divorce.

Paragraph 3 Health Article 18 (1) The Regency Government provides adequate health and maternity facilities for pregnant and breastfeeding mothers.

2. Public service providers must provide special facilities for breastfeeding mothers.

Paragraph 4 Employment Article 19 (1) Employers who employ Women must maintain decency, safety and security while in the workplace.

2. Employers must place female workers in places that are safe for Women's reproductive health.
3. Employers must fulfill the rights of female workers to receive wages in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
4. Employers provide special facilities for breastfeeding mothers in their companies.

Article 20 (1) Female workers/laborers who are at most 18 (eighteen) years old are prohibited from being employed between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB.

2. Employers are prohibited from employing pregnant female workers/laborers who according to a doctor's statement are dangerous to the health and safety of their pregnancy or themselves during working hours from 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB.
3. Employers who employ female workers/laborers between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB, must: a. provide nutritious food and drinks; and b. maintain decency and security while in the workplace. (4) Employers must provide shuttle transportation for female workers/laborers who depart and return from work between 23.00 WIB until 05.00 WIB.

Community Article 10 (1) The community is obliged and responsible in implementing the protection of Women and Children including:

2. The responsibility of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency/City that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 14. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Part One

Definition, Understanding and Terminology Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regency is Musi Banyuasin Regency. 2. Regency Government is the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Musi Banyuasin. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency. 5. Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as DPPPA is the Regional Apparatus that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Musi Banyuasin Regency. 6. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of Women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 9. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 10. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has potential and/or special talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields. 11. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights. 12. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency/City that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 14. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. Women victims of violence are Women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Child victims of violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 20. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement statutory regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards. 25. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop properly. 26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28.

Community Article 10 (1) The community is obliged and responsible in implementing the protection of Women and Children including:

2. The responsibility of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Definition, Understanding and Terminology Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency. 5. Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as DPPPA is the Regional Apparatus that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Musi Banyuasin Regency. 6. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of Women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 9. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 10. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has potential and/or special talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields. 11. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights. 12. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency/City that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 14. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. Women victims of violence are Women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Child victims of violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 20. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement statutory regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards. 25. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop properly. 26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28.

Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. General Article 16 The Regency Government implements the Protection of Women by involving:
a. family;
b. community leaders;
c. religious leaders;
d. community;
e. community organizations in the field of protection of Women.

Paragraph 2 Marriage Article 17 During the marriage bond or after divorce, a Woman has the same rights as the man who is her husband/former husband over all matters relating to the consequences of marriage and/or divorce.

Paragraph 3 Health Article 18 (1) The Regency Government provides adequate health and maternity facilities for pregnant and breastfeeding mothers.

2. Public service providers must provide special facilities for breastfeeding mothers.

Paragraph 4 Employment Article 19 (1) Employers who employ Women must maintain decency, safety and security while in the workplace.

2. Employers must place female workers in places that are safe for Women's reproductive health.
3. Employers must fulfill the rights of female workers to receive wages in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
4. Employers provide special facilities for breastfeeding mothers in their companies.

Article 20 (1) Female workers/laborers who are at most 18 (eighteen) years old are prohibited from being employed between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB.

2. Employers are prohibited from employing pregnant female workers/laborers who according to a doctor's statement are dangerous to the health and safety of their pregnancy or themselves during working hours from 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB.
3. Employers who employ female workers/laborers between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB, must: a. provide nutritious food and drinks; and b. maintain decency and security while in the workplace. (4) Employers must provide shuttle transportation for female workers/laborers who depart and return from work between 23.00 WIB until 05.00 WIB.

Paragraph 5 Education

Part Two

Community Article 10 (1) The community is obliged and responsible in implementing the protection of Women and Children including:
a. participation in prevention and providing support for the development of prevention programs for violations of the rights of Women and Children;
b. providing information and/or reporting violations of the rights of Women and Children to the competent authorities; and c. supervising the law enforcement process against cases of violations of the rights of Women and Children.
2. The responsibility of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

CHAPTER X

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 58 (1) The Regent conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of Protection of Women and Children.

2. The guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be conducted in the form of: a. training for government officials and law enforcement officers on prevention and handling of violence;
b. training for religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against Women and Children;
c. training for health workers who provide health services to Women and Children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units, and general hospitals;
d. training for social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect Women and Children victims of violence; and f. improvement of professionalism of officers, managers of violence case data against Women and Children at community health centers, integrated service units and hospitals.
3. The Regent in conducting guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) may delegate to the Head of Agency.

Article 59 (1) The Head of DPPPA is obliged to submit a report on the implementation of the Women and Children protection program to the Regent.

2. The report as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted periodically 1 (one) time every 3 (three) months.

Article 60 (1) The Regent conducts supervision and evaluation of the implementation of Protection of Women and Children periodically 1 (one) time every 3 (three) months.

2. The results of the evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) constitute evaluation material for the policy of the Women and Children protection program in the Regency.

Complaint handling is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 20. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement statutory regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards. 25. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop properly. 26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28.

2. The responsibility of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Article 21

Women are guaranteed the right to obtain education at every level of formal and non-formal education.

Paragraph 6 Social Article 22 (1) The Regency Government implements empowerment of Women experiencing socio-economic vulnerability through productive economic business activities.

2. Community Organizations may carry out empowerment for Women experiencing socio-economic vulnerability as referred to in paragraph (1) in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations. !

DECIDES:

REGIONAL REGULATION ON THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN'S AND CHILDREN'S RIGHTS. CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Part One

Definition, Understanding and Terminology Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regency is Musi Banyuasin Regency. 2. Regency Government is the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Musi Banyuasin. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency. 5. Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as DPPPA is the Regional Apparatus that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Musi Banyuasin Regency. 6. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of Women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 9. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 10. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has potential and/or special talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields. 11. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights. 12. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency/City that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 14. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. Women victims of violence are Women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Child victims of violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 20. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement statutory regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards. 25. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop properly. 26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28.

Paragraph 1

General Article 16 The Regency Government implements the Protection of Women by involving:
a. family;
b. community leaders;
c. religious leaders;
d. community;
e. community organizations in the field of protection of Women.

Paragraph 2 Marriage Article 17 During the marriage bond or after divorce, a Woman has the same rights as the man who is her husband/former husband over all matters relating to the consequences of marriage and/or divorce.

Paragraph 3 Health Article 18 (1) The Regency Government provides adequate health and maternity facilities for pregnant and breastfeeding mothers.

2. Public service providers must provide special facilities for breastfeeding mothers.

Paragraph 4 Employment Article 19 (1) Employers who employ Women must maintain decency, safety and security while in the workplace.

2. Employers must place female workers in places that are safe for Women's reproductive health.
3. Employers must fulfill the rights of female workers to receive wages in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
4. Employers provide special facilities for breastfeeding mothers in their companies.

Article 20 (1) Female workers/laborers who are at most 18 (eighteen) years old are prohibited from being employed between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB.

2. Employers are prohibited from employing pregnant female workers/laborers who according to a doctor's statement are dangerous to the health and safety of their pregnancy or themselves during working hours from 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB.
3. Employers who employ female workers/laborers between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB, must: a. provide nutritious food and drinks; and b. maintain decency and security while in the workplace. (4) Employers must provide shuttle transportation for female workers/laborers who depart and return from work between 23.00 WIB until 05.00 WIB.

Paragraph 5 Education

Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to recognize power relationship gaps between Women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on Women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of Women and men are different. 29. Public service provider is every state organizing institution, corporation, independent institution formed based on Law for public service activities, and other legal entities formed solely for public service activities. 30. Community Organization is an organization established and formed by the community voluntarily based on common aspirations, will, needs, interests, activities and goals to participate in development for the achievement of the objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila. 31. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 32. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their Child, or father and his Child, or mother and her Child, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 33. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to empower Women in various fields of development, as well as protection of Women and Children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, which is established by the government or community-based.

CHAPTER X

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 58 (1) The Regent conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of Protection of Women and Children.

2. The guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be conducted in the form of: a. training for government officials and law enforcement officers on prevention and handling of violence;
b. training for religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against Women and Children;
c. training for health workers who provide health services to Women and Children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units, and general hospitals;
d. training for social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect Women and Children victims of violence; and f. improvement of professionalism of officers, managers of violence case data against Women and Children at community health centers, integrated service units and hospitals.
3. The Regent in conducting guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) may delegate to the Head of Agency.

Article 59 (1) The Head of DPPPA is obliged to submit a report on the implementation of the Women and Children protection program to the Regent.

2. The report as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted periodically 1 (one) time every 3 (three) months.

Article 60 (1) The Regent conducts supervision and evaluation of the implementation of Protection of Women and Children periodically 1 (one) time every 3 (three) months.

2. The results of the evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) constitute evaluation material for the policy of the Women and Children protection program in the Regency.

CHAPTER XII

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 62 Implementing regulations of this Regional Regulation shall be stipulated no later than 1 (one) year from the promulgation of this Regional Regulation.

Article 63 This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation. In order that everyone may know of it, orders the promulgation of this Regional Regulation by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Musi Banyuasin Regency.
